Posterior benefit-risk score of cohorts

Source: R/BenefitRisk.R
BenefitRisk.Rd

Computes, for each cohort, the posterior probabilities that its endpoints are favorable, the admissibility of the cohort and the composite benefit-risk score of Chakraborty et al. (2026). Without a reference cohort each cohort is assessed against target values; with a reference cohort each other cohort is assessed by its difference from the reference.

Usage

BenefitRisk(
  data,
  endpoints,
  criteria,
  group = "group",
  reference = NULL,
  n.nodes = 200
)

Arguments

data

Patient-level data frame with one row per patient.

endpoints

An Endpoint object or a list of them.

criteria

Data frame of the components; see Details.

group

Name of the column of data with the cohort.

reference

NULL for scores against target values, or the cohort used as the reference.

n.nodes

Number of Gauss-Legendre nodes for probabilities of differences.

Value

A data frame of class BenefitRisk with one row per cohort (other than the reference) and columns group, reference (with a reference cohort), one column per component with its posterior probability, admissible, BR and, without a reference cohort, selected. The attribute components holds the definition, weight and cutoff of each component, and the attribute reference the reference cohort (if any). See BenefitRisk-methods for print() and plot().

Details

Components. Each row of criteria defines a component S_k: the posterior probability that the parameter of an endpoint is favorable (see PosteriorProb). For a binary endpoint the parameter is the rate, with a beta prior and a binomial likelihood. For a time-to-event endpoint the event times are taken as exponential, with a gamma prior of the hazard; the parameter is the survival probability at time (measure = "surv") or, with a reference cohort, the hazard ratio (measure = "hr"). Without a reference cohort, a component is P(parameter >= target) for a favorable direction higher.better = TRUE of the endpoint and P(parameter <= target) otherwise; with a reference cohort, it is the probability that the difference from the reference is at least target (or at most target), or that the hazard ratio is at most target. A median can be assessed through the survival probability at the target median with target = 0.5.

Columns of criteria.

  • endpoint (required): the name of an endpoint in endpoints. An endpoint can appear in several components, for example the survival probabilities at two times.

  • target (required): the target value or margin.

  • measure: "rate" (binary endpoints), "surv" or "hr" (time-to-event endpoints); by default "rate" and "surv".

  • time: the time of the survival probability.

  • weight: the exponent of the component in the composite score; by default 1 / K for K components.

  • cutoff: the admissibility cutoff of the component, or NA for none.

  • prior.a, prior.b: the parameters of the prior: beta shape parameters (default 0.5 and 0.5), or gamma shape and rate of the hazard (default 0.5 and 0).

  • label: the name of the component in the output; by default the endpoint name, followed by _S and the time for survival probabilities (for example PFS_S6) and by _HR for hazard ratios.

Composite score and admissibility. The benefit-risk score is BR = prod(S_k ^ weight_k). With equal weights summing to 1 it is the geometric mean of the components. The score of Chakraborty et al. (2026), the geometric mean of the efficacy components times the geometric mean of the safety components, is obtained with weights 1 / K_efficacy and 1 / K_safety. A cohort is admissible when every component with a cutoff satisfies S_k >= cutoff_k; the cutoff of a safety component of the form P(Delta >= t) < p in Chakraborty et al. (2026) is 1 - p. Without a reference cohort, the admissible cohort with the highest score is marked as selected.

References

Chakraborty, S., Dubey, A. K., Kumar, A. and Chan, I. (2026). A two-stage dose optimization framework for oncology drug development with multiple efficacy and safety endpoints via an integrated benefit-risk assessment. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, published online. doi:10.1080/19466315.2026.2668381

See also

PosteriorProb, WinStat, SimSelection

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(group = rep(c("Cohort1", "Cohort2"), each = 40),
                pfs_tte = rexp(80, log(2) / rep(c(8, 6), each = 40)),
                pfs_event = 1,
                response = rbinom(80, 1, rep(c(0.45, 0.30), each = 40)),
                ae = rbinom(80, 1, rep(c(0.35, 0.20), each = 40)))
eps <- list(Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),
            Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),
            Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE))

# against target values
crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "AE"), target = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.3),
                   time = c(NA, 6, NA), cutoff = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
BenefitRisk(d, eps, crit)
#> Posterior benefit-risk scores against target values
#> 
#>  component definition     weight cutoff
#>  ORR       P(rate >= 0.3) 0.333  0.5   
#>  PFS_S6    P(S(6) >= 0.5) 0.333  0.5   
#>  AE        P(rate <= 0.3) 0.333  0.5   
#> 
#>    group   ORR PFS_S6    AE admissible    BR selected
#>  Cohort1 0.996  0.955 0.627       TRUE 0.842     TRUE
#>  Cohort2 0.509  0.869 0.995       TRUE 0.761    FALSE
#> 
#> Selected: Cohort1

# Cohort1 relative to Cohort2
crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "AE"),
                       measure = c("rate", "hr", "rate"),
                       target = c(0.1, 0.8, 0.1))
BenefitRisk(d, eps, crit_ref, reference = "Cohort2")
#> Posterior benefit-risk scores relative to Cohort2
#> 
#>  component definition                weight cutoff
#>  ORR       P(rate - rate_ref >= 0.1) 0.333        
#>  PFS_HR    P(HR <= 0.8)              0.333        
#>  AE        P(rate - rate_ref <= 0.1) 0.333        
#> 
#>    group reference   ORR PFS_HR    AE admissible    BR
#>  Cohort1   Cohort2 0.817  0.266 0.296       TRUE 0.401
